terms.gloss: equally; aequē ac (atque), just as … as
evidence: Cic. Fin. 1.65: laetāmur amīcōrum laetitiā aequē atque nostrā (Lewis & Short)
Sen. Ep. 91.17: omnibus eadem sunt, aequē difficilia
terms.comment: “Just as much as” is aequē ac, aequē atque; in comedy aequē also takes cum or the ablative (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: equally, alike; together, at the same time
evidence: Cic. Fin. 1.65: pariter dolēmus angōribus (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 2.30: cāritāte nōn pariter omnēs egēmus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “In the same way, alike”; it very often means “together, at the same time” (pariter cum, together with), as in the loci from Pliny and Quintilian (audīvī pariter et vīdī, Plin. Ep. 8.20.3).

terms.gloss: equally, in equal shares, on equal terms
terms.grammar: phrase: ex with the ablative of aequum
evidence: Sen. Ep. 66.26: avēs ex aequō partiuntur cibōs
terms.comment: Of sharing and of standing: “in equal measure, on an equal footing” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: laetāmur amīcōrum laetitiā aequē atque nostrā, et pariter dolēmus angōribus
phrases.english: we are glad at our friends’ joy just as at our own, and grieve equally at their troubles

phrases.latin: ‘facilia’ inquit ‘mē docē’. cui praeceptor ‘ista’ inquit ‘omnibus eadem sunt, aequē difficilia’
phrases.english: “Teach me the easy things,” he said. His teacher answered, “These are the same for everyone, equally hard.”

phrases.latin: fētūs suōs nōn distinguunt ferae et sē in alimentum pariter omnium sternunt; avēs ex aequō partiuntur cibōs
phrases.english: wild animals make no difference between their young and lie down to feed them all alike; birds share the food out equally

phrases.latin: Prōdesse quī vult nec potest, aequē est miser.
phrases.english: He who wants to help and cannot is just as unhappy.

sources: Lewis & Short: aeque · Lewis & Short: aequus · Lewis & Short: pariter · Lewis & Short: par
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-publilius, loci-plinius), checked against the editions named there.
Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 310.
